findings.finding: Reported net loss is unlikely to narrow against the year-ago $(1,294,700) even though $603,200 of year-ago interest expense is gone: the year-ago quarter carried an income-tax benefit (25.8% effective rate in Q1 FY26) that no longer exists because a valuation allowance now offsets the NOL benefit (Q1 FY27 tax expense $16,500 on a $1.38m pre-tax loss), and the Hilti Complex rental income that sat in 'other income' ($619,500 in Q1 FY26) went with the building sale (Q1 FY27 'other' was a $103,700 expense); on Q1 FY27 opex run-rates (O&S $0.68m, commissions ~29% of PaperPie revenue, G&A $2.07m) and ~$4.2m of revenue at 58% gross margin, the pre-tax loss is about $(1.4)-(1.6)m, EPS around $(0.16)-(0.19) against $(0.15).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-07-09: net loss widened to $(1.40)m from $(1.08)m on the same tax and other-income swing and the stock fell 3.18%; 2026-05-19 (Q4 FY26 loss $(3.1)m with a $1.5m valuation allowance) fell 3.36%.

findings.finding: Usborne, 33% of PaperPie revenue in Q1 FY27 (48% in the year-ago Q2), can terminate the distribution agreement on under 30 days' notice: the 10-Q states the company did not meet minimum purchase volumes and 'did not supply the letter of credit required under the Agreement', Usborne has refused a $1.0m FY22 volume rebate, and Usborne purchases were $0 in the quarter; the Q2 10-Q is the next place a termination notice or a further cut in Usborne share would appear.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print has carried a Usborne termination; the same disclosure has sat in every 10-Q and the 10-K (filed 2026-05-19) without a notice, and those prints moved -0.7% to -3.4%.

findings.finding: Publishing faces an inflated comp: the year-ago Q2 FY26 Publishing revenue of $889,900 was lifted by 'additional discounts offered to retail customers in the second quarter of fiscal 2026 to spur sales' (10-Q), and Publishing was already down 40% YoY in Q1 FY27 ($580,900 vs $1,046,100); a repeat of that rate puts Publishing near $0.55m, about $0.35m or 7.5% of total year-ago revenue.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Publishing is ~15% of revenue; no print has visibly traded on it.
